facts.text: Geistown’s first settlers, the Adams family, arrived in 1769 before official permission, setting the stage for the borough’s early frontier life.
The Slick family’s 1812 farm, later called Slicksville, housed the first Methodist church in Geistown when it opened on December 25, 1829.
A hidden stop on the Underground Railroad, the Slick farm and tannery helped free enslaved people travel northward from Geistown.
Early Geistown entrepreneurs saw the automobile’s promise and opened gasoline stations, making the town a roadside service hub in the early 20th century.
Geistown sits at 40°17′40″N 78°52′26″W, placing it in southwestern Cambria County just 4 miles southeast of downtown Johnstown.
